spec.description: Accessibility in Cuenca with R5 (Conveyal): from two draggable origins, A and B, travelling the same way, and from A in two scenarios set in a form (bike against walk and transit by default, with or without the terrain's slope). The browser compares them with Chaski and Mosaic: every street coloured by who gets there sooner, the people, area, stops and parks within reach, the schools, hospitals, parks and shopping centres reached, all played minute by minute from a 07:00 departure with the Time Brush.

options.content:
**Two comparisons, one per tab.** *Who gets there first* puts two places side by side: drag marker A or marker B anywhere in Cuenca, and both travel the way the form above the map says. *Two ways from A* keeps one place and compares two ways of travelling from it, set in its form: by default scenario 1 is the bike, door to door, and scenario 2 is walking with the buses and the tram. Change the form and press Apply: R5 computes the new travel times in about a second, once for all the changes. **Press play on the Time Brush** to watch both journeys spread minute by minute from a 07:00 departure, or drag the end of its window to stop at a minute: the maps, the figures and the Mosaic charts of both tabs keep what is reached by then, all in the browser. The cutoff and the service day at the top apply to both tabs.

**Travel times** come from [R5](https://github.com/conveyal/r5), Conveyal's routing engine, running for Cuenca on Ubica's servers with OpenStreetMap streets and the GTFS of the city's 37 bus routes and its tram, for the service day chosen (2 September 2026 by default). R5 answers for departures between 07:00 and 09:00 and keeps the median of 200 draws, so a time already includes a typical wait. Its answer is a grid of cells of about 153 m (Web Mercator zoom 10). The minute shown is R5's minute plus one: R5 counts a cell within 30 minutes when it is reached in less than 30. With slope, R5 applies Tobler's hiking function on Cuenca's 10 m terrain model to the walking parts of the trip (to the stop, from it, between rides). A small service, iso-cuenca, turns R5's binary answer into rows DuckDB can read; the gateway caches each answer for a month (`/r5/`).

**People** are LlactaLAB's (Universidad de Cuenca) population per building, Google Open Buildings with population disaggregated to each building, the same layer R5's own accessibility counts are built from: summed per cell, they come within 2 % of R5's count at every minute. **Parks** are LlactaLAB's 381 parks by their entrances (reserves left out), reached at the first. **Transit stops** are those of the GTFS R5 routes on. **Streets**, **schools**, **hospitals** and **shopping centres** are from [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org) (release 2026-10-21, from OpenStreetMap, ODbL): land use of hospitals, schools and colleges, and shopping centres by name. All of it is joined to R5's cells by their column and row, in `datasets/cuenca-access/build.sh`, which each instance runs once.

**How it is built.** The server reads R5's cells for A and B through the gateway into a Chaski dataset, with the people of each cell; the streets and the places load once per visit. Everything else is DuckDB-WASM in the browser: the comparison cell by cell, the streets joined to their cells, the places each run reaches, the figures. Each street piece takes its cell's minutes, so the streets show the travel times R5 computed on OpenStreetMap at Overture's geometry; a street inside an unreached cell stays dark even if it is close. The Time Brush (Kepler Plus) is a clause on the time column of a Mosaic selection, `clock`, that the kepler maps filter on the GPU and the Mosaic charts follow; its window also reaches the figures through Chaski's filters. This dashboard needs the R5 instance of Cuenca, which only pacha.ubica.dev has.

spec.rawSql:
-- The Time Brush's track: people reached in each minute after the 07:00
-- departure (the bar at 07:09 is those within 10 minutes but not 9), from a
-- and from b, from 07:00 to the cutoff. It reads no window, so dragging
-- does not ask it again.
WITH m AS (
  SELECT (coalesce(try_cast($date AS DATE), DATE '2026-09-02') + INTERVAL 7 HOUR + range * INTERVAL 1 MINUTE)::TIMESTAMP AS time
  FROM range(0, coalesce(try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER), 30) + 1)
)
SELECT m.time,
       coalesce(sum(c.population) FILTER (WHERE c.origin = 'A'), 0)::DOUBLE AS "People reached, from a",
       coalesce(sum(c.population) FILTER (WHERE c.origin = 'B'), 0)::DOUBLE AS "People reached, from b"
FROM m
LEFT JOIN $cells AS c ON c.time = m.time
GROUP BY m.time
ORDER BY m.time

spec.description: People newly within reach in each minute after leaving at 07:00, from a (area) and from b (line). The window starts at the departure; drag its end, or press play, and every map, chart and figure on both tabs keeps what is reached by then. The bar stays pinned at the top once the panel scrolls away.
spec.title: The clock: minutes after a 07:00 departure

spec.rawSql:
-- The Time Brush's track: people reached in each minute after the 07:00
-- departure (the bar at 07:09 is those within 10 minutes but not 9), scenario 1
-- and scenario 2, from 07:00 to the cutoff. It reads no window, so dragging
-- does not ask it again.
WITH m AS (
  SELECT (coalesce(try_cast($date AS DATE), DATE '2026-09-02') + INTERVAL 7 HOUR + range * INTERVAL 1 MINUTE)::TIMESTAMP AS time
  FROM range(0, coalesce(try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER), 30) + 1)
)
SELECT m.time,
       coalesce(sum(c.population) FILTER (WHERE c.scenario = '1'), 0)::DOUBLE AS "People reached, scenario 1",
       coalesce(sum(c.population) FILTER (WHERE c.scenario = '2'), 0)::DOUBLE AS "People reached, scenario 2"
FROM m
LEFT JOIN $modes AS c ON c.time = m.time
GROUP BY m.time
ORDER BY m.time

spec.description: People newly within reach in each minute after leaving at 07:00, scenario 1 (area) and scenario 2 (line). The bar stays pinned at the top once the panel scrolls away.

spec.rawSql:
-- The whole curve, not the window: people, area, transit stops and parks within
-- reach of each run by each minute after 07:00, up to the cutoff. It reads no
-- window; the chart draws the window's end from the variable.
WITH m AS (SELECT range::DOUBLE AS minute FROM range(0, coalesce(try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER), 30) + 1)),
o AS (SELECT unnest(['A', 'B']) AS side),
g AS (SELECT o.side, m.minute FROM o, m),
c AS (SELECT origin AS side, minutes, sum(population) AS people, sum(km2) AS km2 FROM $cells GROUP BY ALL),
r AS (
  SELECT origin AS side, minutes,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'Transit stop') AS stops, count(*) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'Park') AS parks
  FROM $reached
  GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT g.side, g.minute,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(people), 0) FROM c WHERE c.side = g.side AND c.minutes <= g.minute)::DOUBLE AS people,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(km2), 0) FROM c WHERE c.side = g.side AND c.minutes <= g.minute)::DOUBLE AS km2,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(stops), 0) FROM r WHERE r.side = g.side AND r.minutes <= g.minute)::DOUBLE AS stops,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(parks), 0) FROM r WHERE r.side = g.side AND r.minutes <= g.minute)::DOUBLE AS parks
FROM g
ORDER BY g.side, g.minute

spec.description: People, area, transit stops and parks within reach from a and from b by each minute after 07:00, up to the cutoff. The dashed line is the end of the Time Brush window.
spec.title: Within reach, minute by minute

-- The whole curve, not the window: people, area, transit stops and parks within

WITH m AS (SELECT range::DOUBLE AS minute FROM range(0, coalesce(try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER), 30) + 1)),
o AS (SELECT unnest(['1', '2']) AS side),
g AS (SELECT o.side, m.minute FROM o, m),
c AS (SELECT scenario AS side, minutes, sum(population) AS people, sum(km2) AS km2 FROM $modes GROUP BY ALL),
r AS (
  SELECT scenario AS side, minutes,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'Transit stop') AS stops, count(*) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'Park') AS parks
  FROM $reached_m
  GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT g.side, g.minute,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(people), 0) FROM c WHERE c.side = g.side AND c.minutes <= g.minute)::DOUBLE AS people,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(km2), 0) FROM c WHERE c.side = g.side AND c.minutes <= g.minute)::DOUBLE AS km2,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(stops), 0) FROM r WHERE r.side = g.side AND r.minutes <= g.minute)::DOUBLE AS stops,
       (SELECT coalesce(sum(parks), 0) FROM r WHERE r.side = g.side AND r.minutes <= g.minute)::DOUBLE AS parks

ORDER BY g.side, g.minute

spec.rawSql:
-- Every piece of street in a cell reached from A, at the minute A reaches
-- it: the streets are Overture's, cut at the edges of R5's cells, so each piece
-- takes its cell's minutes. The other marker's streets are the map's other
-- dataset, drawn additively, so where both reach the two colours add up. The
-- Time Brush window filters them in kepler, each on its own arrival time.
SELECT s.class, c.minutes, c.time, s.geometry
FROM $streets AS s
JOIN $cells AS c USING (px, py)
WHERE c.origin = 'A'

-- Every piece of street in a cell reached from B, at the minute B reaches
-- it: the streets are Overture's, cut at the edges of R5's cells, so each piece
-- takes its cell's minutes. The other marker's streets are the map's other
-- dataset, drawn additively, so where both reach the two colours add up. The
-- Time Brush window filters them in kepler, each on its own arrival time.
SELECT s.class, c.minutes, c.time, s.geometry
FROM $streets AS s
JOIN $cells AS c USING (px, py)
WHERE c.origin = 'B'

spec.description: Every piece of street in a cell of R5's grid (about 153 m) reached within the cutoff, from marker A in blue and from marker B in orange, drawn additively: where both markers reach a street the colours add up towards white, so the shared part of the city stands out from what only one reaches. Each network grows on its own clock with the Time Brush. Who gets there sooner, and by how much, is in the charts beside. Drag A or B to move an origin: R5 answers in about a second.
spec.title: Two networks: every street reached from A (blue) and from B (orange); white where both reach

spec.rawSql:
-- Every piece of street in a cell either run reaches, coloured by who gets there
-- sooner and by how much (from compare_m): the streets are Overture's,
-- cut at the edges of R5's cells, so each piece takes its cell's minutes. The
-- Time Brush window filters them in kepler, on the GPU (Mosaic selection
-- clock), so a play asks nothing again.
SELECT s.class, c.sooner, c.minutes_x AS minutes_S1, c.minutes_y AS minutes_S2, c.time, s.geometry
FROM $streets AS s
JOIN $compare_m AS c USING (px, py)

-- The cells themselves, faint under the streets: the area each run covers,
-- parks and open ground included, in the same colours.
SELECT sooner, minutes_x AS minutes_S1, minutes_y AS minutes_S2, round(population)::DOUBLE AS people, time, geometry
FROM $compare_m

spec.description: Every piece of street reached from marker A within the cutoff in either scenario (the form above), by how the second scenario compares with the first: magenta where only scenario 2 reaches it and purple where it gets there sooner (gained), lime where only scenario 1 reaches it and green where scenario 1 is sooner (lost); streets both reach in the same minute are dimmed, so what changes stands out. A street appears at the minute the first of the two arrives. Drag A to move the origin of both.
spec.title: What scenario 2 gains and loses against scenario 1, street by street

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: every road of Cuenca in Overture Maps, cut at
-- the edges of R5's cells (datasets/cuenca-access, built per instance), with
-- the cell each piece lies in. Simplified to 2 m and rounded to 1 m, which the
-- map cannot tell apart at street scale and which halves what the browser loads.
SELECT px::DOUBLE AS px, py::DOUBLE AS py, class,
       ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_ReducePrecision(ST_Simplify(geometry, 0.00002), 0.00001))::VARCHAR AS geometry
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/cuenca-access/streets.parquet')
WHERE NOT ST_IsEmpty(ST_ReducePrecision(ST_Simplify(geometry, 0.00002), 0.00001))

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: the places the dashboard measures reach to
-- (datasets/cuenca-access): transit stops of the GTFS R5 routes on, park
-- entrances (LlactaLAB; a park's entrances share its id), and the hospitals,
-- schools and shopping centres of Overture Maps, one row per place and cell
-- of R5's grid it touches, with a point on it to draw.
SELECT id, kind, name, px::DOUBLE AS px, py::DOUBLE AS py, latitude, longitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/cuenca-access/places.parquet')

-- Server side, once per pair of origins: R5's travel times from markers A and
-- B, both travelling as the form of the first tab says, through the gateway's http://feeds/r5/
-- (iso-cuenca, the bridge to the R5 instance of Cuenca; a month's cache per
-- query): one row per run and cell of R5's grid (zoom 10, about 153 m) reached
-- within the cutoff, with the people LlactaLAB counts in it
-- (datasets/cuenca-access).
-- minutes is R5's whole minute plus one: R5 counts a cell within m minutes when
-- it is reached in less than m, so a cell it times at 29 is within 30. time is
-- the start of the minute R5 reaches it in, after a 07:00 departure on the
-- service day: the clock the Time Brush plays, whose window [07:00, 07:30)
-- then holds exactly what is within 30 minutes (R5 itself takes the median
-- over departures from 07:00 to 09:00). px and py are the cell's column and
-- row, which the browser joins the streets and the places on. Origins are kept
-- inside R5's extent and rounded to four decimals (11 m), as iso-cuenca does,
-- so a marker dropped where it was finds the cache.
SET VARIABLE run_A = 'http://feeds/r5/cells.json?lat=' || round(greatest(-3.02, least(-2.76, coalesce(try_cast($alat AS DOUBLE), -2.8975))), 4)
  || '&lon=' || round(greatest(-79.11, least(-78.87, coalesce(try_cast($alng AS DOUBLE), -79.0044))), 4)
  || '&date=' || strftime(coalesce(try_cast($date AS DATE), DATE '2026-09-02'), '%Y-%m-%d')
  || '&calle=' || $street || '&transit=${transit:csv}' || '&walk=' || $walk || '&rides=' || $rides
  || '&bundle=' || $network || '&max=' || (coalesce(try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER), 30) - 1);
SET VARIABLE run_B = 'http://feeds/r5/cells.json?lat=' || round(greatest(-3.02, least(-2.76, coalesce(try_cast($blat AS DOUBLE), -2.8921))), 4)
  || '&lon=' || round(greatest(-79.11, least(-78.87, coalesce(try_cast($blng AS DOUBLE), -78.979))), 4)
  || '&date=' || strftime(coalesce(try_cast($date AS DATE), DATE '2026-09-02'), '%Y-%m-%d')
  || '&calle=' || $street || '&transit=${transit:csv}' || '&walk=' || $walk || '&rides=' || $rides
  || '&bundle=' || $network || '&max=' || (coalesce(try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER), 30) - 1);
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT 'A' AS side, minutos, geom FROM read_json(getvariable('run_A'), columns = {'minutos': 'INTEGER', 'geom': 'VARCHAR'})
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'B' AS side, minutos, geom FROM read_json(getvariable('run_B'), columns = {'minutos': 'INTEGER', 'geom': 'VARCHAR'})
),
cell AS (
  SELECT side, minutos + 1 AS minutes, geom, ST_Centroid(ST_GeomFromHEXWKB(geom)) AS c FROM raw
),
grid AS (
  -- R5's cells are Web Mercator pixels: 262,144 across the world at zoom 10.
  SELECT side, minutes, geom,
         floor((ST_X(c) + 180) / 360 * 262144)::INTEGER AS px,
         floor((1 - ln(tan(radians(ST_Y(c))) + 1 / cos(radians(ST_Y(c)))) / pi()) / 2 * 262144)::INTEGER AS py,
         pow(40075016.686 / 262144 * cos(radians(ST_Y(c))), 2) / 1e6 AS km2
  FROM cell
)
SELECT g.side AS origin, g.px::DOUBLE AS px, g.py::DOUBLE AS py, g.minutes::DOUBLE AS minutes,
       (coalesce(try_cast($date AS DATE), DATE '2026-09-02') + INTERVAL 7 HOUR + (g.minutes - 1) * INTERVAL 1 MINUTE)::TIMESTAMP AS time,
       coalesce(p.population, 0)::DOUBLE AS population, round(g.km2, 5)::DOUBLE AS km2, g.geom AS geometry
FROM grid AS g
LEFT JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/cuenca-access/population.parquet') AS p USING (px, py)
ORDER BY time, origin

spec.description: One row per cell either run reaches (markers A and B), with the minutes from each and who gets there first.
spec.name: compare

source.sql:
-- In the browser, from cells: one row per cell either run reaches, with
-- the minutes from each, the lead (the minutes of B less those of A: above
-- zero A gets there sooner; a cell one run does not reach within the cutoff
-- counts as reached by it a minute after the cutoff) and who is sooner in nine
-- classes, the charts' colours: a cell only one run reaches is a class of its
-- own, apart from those both reach. time is the first arrival.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT px, py, any_value(geometry) AS geometry, any_value(population) AS population, any_value(km2) AS km2,
         min(minutes) FILTER (WHERE origin = 'A') AS minutes_x,
         min(minutes) FILTER (WHERE origin = 'B') AS minutes_y,
         min(time) AS time
  FROM $cells
  GROUP BY px, py
),
l AS (
  SELECT *, coalesce(minutes_y, try_cast($cutoff AS DOUBLE) + 1) - coalesce(minutes_x, try_cast($cutoff AS DOUBLE) + 1) AS lead
  FROM w
)
SELECT px, py, minutes_x, minutes_y, lead, population, km2, time, geometry,
       CASE WHEN minutes_y IS NULL THEN 'Only A' WHEN minutes_x IS NULL THEN 'Only B'
            WHEN lead >= 10 THEN 'A by 10+ min' WHEN lead >= 5 THEN 'A by 5–9 min' WHEN lead >= 1 THEN 'A by 1–4 min'
            WHEN lead = 0 THEN 'Same minute' WHEN lead > -5 THEN 'B by 1–4 min' WHEN lead > -10 THEN 'B by 5–9 min'
            ELSE 'B by 10+ min' END AS sooner
FROM l
ORDER BY time

-- In the browser, from places and cells: one row per run and place it
-- reaches within the cutoff, at the first of the place's cells it reaches (a
-- park at its first entrance).
SELECT c.origin, p.id, any_value(p.kind) AS kind, any_value(p.name) AS name,
       any_value(p.latitude) AS latitude, any_value(p.longitude) AS longitude,
       min(c.minutes) AS minutes, min(c.time) AS time
FROM $places AS p
JOIN $cells AS c USING (px, py)
GROUP BY c.origin, p.id
ORDER BY time

source.sql:
-- In the browser, from reached: one row per place either run reaches,
-- with the minutes from each, the first arrival (time), and the lead (minutes
-- of the second run less those of the first, capped at 30 either way; a run
-- that does not reach it counts as a minute after the cutoff).
SELECT id, any_value(kind) AS kind, any_value(name) AS name,
       any_value(latitude) AS latitude, any_value(longitude) AS longitude,
       min(minutes) FILTER (WHERE origin = 'A') AS minutes_x,
       min(minutes) FILTER (WHERE origin = 'B') AS minutes_y,
       min(time) AS time,
       greatest(-30, least(30,
         coalesce(min(minutes) FILTER (WHERE origin = 'B'), try_cast($cutoff AS DOUBLE) + 1)
         - coalesce(min(minutes) FILTER (WHERE origin = 'A'), try_cast($cutoff AS DOUBLE) + 1))) AS lead
FROM $reached
GROUP BY id
ORDER BY time

-- In the browser, from modes: one row per cell either run reaches, with
